name: Streaming Media Lens
description: This whitepaper describes the AWS Streaming Media Lens for the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which helps customers apply best practices in the design, delivery, and maintenance of their cloud-based streaming media workloads. The document describes general design principles, as well as specific best practices and guidance for the six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework.

questions.title: How does your organization support streaming media outcomes?
questions.description: Streaming workflows cross multiple teams (encoding, delivery, client, and operations) and require clear ownership at each stage.

choices.title: Assess trade-offs between streaming architecture options and associated risks

helpfulResource.displayText: When designing streaming video infrastructure, carefully evaluate the trade-offs between different architectural approaches and their associated risks. This includes considering factors such as performance, scalability, availability, security, and cost to determine the optimal solution for different streaming scenarios.

improvementPlan.displayText: Assess trade-offs between streaming architecture options and associated risks

choices.title: Create RACI matrices for streaming video operations

helpfulResource.displayText: Define clear roles and responsibilities for each stakeholder involved in streaming video operations. By implementing RACI (responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed) matrices, organizations can establish a clear framework for accountability and decision-making across the entire streaming workflow.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create RACI matrices for streaming video operations

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this if your workload does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: How do you achieve full observability across your streaming video workflow?
questions.description: Streaming workflows are distributed systems spanning ingest, processing, origin, CDN, and client. Detecting, diagnosing, and resolving issues requires visibility into metrics, events, and dependencies across all of these layers.

choices.title: Establish performance metrics by defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and service-level objectives (SLOs)

helpfulResource.displayText: Establishing a full set of operational performance metrics is critical in streaming video workloads. It helps organizations to measure, monitor, and validate the performance of streaming operations across different scenarios.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish performance metrics by defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and service-level objectives (SLOs)

choices.title: Implement comprehensive monitoring and collect granular metrics across all layers of your streaming stack

helpfulResource.displayText: Streaming video workloads require a complete approach to monitoring that spans all layers of the streaming stack i.e., infrastructure, encoding, packaging, delivery, and playback while collecting granular, scenario-specific metrics with near real-time latency. By combining full stack-wide monitoring with advanced analytics and anomaly detection, you can proactively identify and resolve issues before they impact viewer experience, even during high-demand periods.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement comprehensive monitoring and collect granular metrics across all layers of your streaming stack

choices.title: Implement centralized logging to aggregate logs from all components of your streaming stack

helpfulResource.displayText: To provide full visibility and operational efficiency across your streaming video stack, implement a centralized logging solution. By aggregating logs from all components of your streaming stack, including third-party integrations and custom applications, you gain a complete view of your system's performance and behavior.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement centralized logging to aggregate logs from all components of your streaming stack

choices.title: Instrument your streaming application code and infrastructure for observability

helpfulResource.displayText: Instrument your streaming application code and infrastructure to emit detailed, structured logs and metrics to achieve full visibility into streaming video workloads. This structured approach enables teams to detect, diagnose, and resolve issues quickly, optimizing performance and reliability of streaming video delivery.

improvementPlan.displayText: Instrument your streaming application code and infrastructure for observability

questions.title: How do you prepare for large-scale streaming media events?
questions.description: Large-scale events involve sudden spikes in viewership that stress every component. Preparation before the event determines whether it delivers without degradation.

choices.title: Implement thorough capacity planning for high-viewership events

helpfulResource.displayText: Large-scale streaming events require thorough capacity planning across all components of the streaming workflow to maintain reliable delivery during peak viewership. This planning must account for potential viewership patterns, regional distribution, and engagement behaviors.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement thorough capacity planning for high-viewership events

choices.title: Conduct thorough pre-event testing for large-scale streaming events

helpfulResource.displayText: Before high-profile streaming events, conduct thorough testing to validate the entire workflow's capacity, reliability, and performance under expected load conditions. This testing helps identify potential issues before they impact viewers during the actual event.

improvementPlan.displayText: Conduct thorough pre-event testing for large-scale streaming events

choices.title: Establish war room and incident readiness procedures for high-profile events

helpfulResource.displayText: During large-scale streaming events, establish dedicated war room and incident readiness procedures that coordinate response and drive rapid resolution of any issues. This approach enables structured decision-making and clear communication during critical streaming periods.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish war room and incident readiness procedures for high-profile events

choices.title: Use specialized media support solutions for business-critical streaming events

helpfulResource.displayText: For business-critical streaming workloads and high-profile live events, use AWS Unified Operations for Media Support Solution (MSS) to augment your operational capabilities with proactive monitoring, specialized media expertise, and accelerated incident response with defined service-level objectives (SLOs).

improvementPlan.displayText: Use specialized media support solutions for business-critical streaming events

questions.description: Streaming systems are susceptible to encoding failures, delivery issues, and quality degradation. Documented, repeatable response procedures reduce resolution time and limit viewer impact during incidents.

choices.title: Create runbooks for common streaming video operational events

helpfulResource.displayText: Develop incident response runbooks that provide a structured framework to manage common operational events and incidents in streaming video workflows. These playbooks outline step-by-step procedures tailored to specific types of incidents, which helps your teams act swiftly and consistently and reduces the likelihood of human error.

questions.title: How do you authorize access to content and content ingest?
questions.description: Authentication and authorization systems control who can access content and how. This covers viewer-facing identity (subscription tiers, geo-restrictions) and infrastructure-level access (origin restrictions, CDN authentication).

choices.title: Use an identity provider to authenticate viewers and access policies to implement least privilege access to protected content

helpfulResource.displayText: Protect content and infrastructure from access by outside personnel, as unauthorized access could lead to content theft. Even internal access should be controlled to reduce the risk of unauthorized access or accidental deletion or loss of data.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use an identity provider to authenticate viewers and access policies to implement least privilege access to protected content

choices.title: Restrict content origin access to allow only authorized content distribution networks

helpfulResource.displayText: Even authenticated users can act maliciously with your workloads, so consider how to secure the data path of your video streams. Tokenization schemes such as signed-URLs, signed-cookies, or JWTs (JSON Web Tokens) should be used to grant only temporary access to content by approved frontend applications. Amazon CloudFront can protect access to content origin through signed URLs and signed cookies with a short duration to live, and Lambda@Edge can validate bearer tokens during viewer request.

improvementPlan.displayText: Restrict content origin access to allow only authorized content distribution networks

choices.title: Monitor for fraudulent access attempts

questions.title: How do you protect content ingest endpoints?

questions.description: Content origins need protection from DDoS attacks at both network and application layers, unauthorized direct access bypassing the CDN, and application-level exploits.

choices.title: Use distributed denial of service (DDoS) protection service to maintain content availability

questions.title: How do you optimize storage and data transfer costs for your streaming media workload?
questions.description: Storage and data transfer often represent the largest cost components. A strategy for lifecycle management and edge caching reduces these costs while maintaining access performance.

choices.title: Implement lifecycle management for media assets

helpfulResource.displayText: Media assets can reach hundreds of gigabytes per file. Without active lifecycle management, storage costs grow linearly with content volume regardless of whether assets are still accessed. Organizations that produce or acquire content continuously accumulate source, mezzanine, and distribution files that remain in high-cost storage tiers long after their access frequency drops to near zero.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement lifecycle management for media assets

choices.title: Optimize content delivery using edge caching and just-in-time packaging

helpfulResource.displayText: Content delivery is typically the largest cost component for organizations streaming to large audiences. A 60-minute video streamed to 1,000 concurrent viewers can generate over 2,700 GB of data transfer per hour. Reducing how often content is fetched from origin and how much content needs to be stored in multiple formats directly reduces this cost while improving viewer experience through lower latency.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize content delivery using edge caching and just-in-time packaging

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this if your workload does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: How do you optimize content processing costs for your streaming media workload?
questions.description: Processing costs scale with encoding volume, instance selection, and utilization efficiency. Baseline measurement, parallel processing, and capacity reservations are the main ways to reduce them.

choices.title: Establish baseline metrics for media processing tasks

helpfulResource.displayText: Consumer demand for more content at higher resolution and quality puts ongoing pressure on processing infrastructure. As transcoding, quality control, and packaging workloads grow, so do their costs. Without measured baselines, teams can't distinguish between expected cost growth and inefficiency, can't forecast accurately, and can't evaluate whether infrastructure changes improve or degrade cost performance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish baseline metrics for media processing tasks

choices.title: Implement parallel processing for media tasks

helpfulResource.displayText: Media processing tasks are inherently parallelizable. Video content can be split on I-frame boundaries, processed as independent segments, and reassembled. Sequential processing on vertically-scaled instances limits you to expensive large instance types and means a single interruption wastes the entire job. Parallel processing across many smaller workers accesses cheaper compute, completes faster, and limits the scope of impact of any single failure.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement parallel processing for media tasks

choices.title: Optimize AWS Elemental Media Services pricing models

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Elemental Media Services offer multiple pricing models that deliver significant savings over on-demand rates when matched to appropriate workload patterns. Organizations that run all workloads at on-demand rates without evaluating reservations, tier selection, or infrastructure lifecycle management leave substantial savings unrealized. Selecting the right pricing model for each workload pattern requires understanding usage characteristics and commitment trade-offs.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize AWS Elemental Media Services pricing models

questions.title: How do you optimize distribution costs while maintaining video quality?
questions.description: Encoding decisions directly determine delivery cost. Lower bit rate at equivalent quality means fewer bytes to store and transfer. Content-aware encoding matches spend to complexity rather than applying uniform high bitrates.

choices.title: Implement thorough video quality assessment

helpfulResource.displayText: Every bit saved in encoding translates directly to reduced delivery cost. A 20 percent bit rate reduction across a content catalog means 20 percent lower CDN spend. The challenge is identifying where those bits can be removed without degrading what viewers actually perceive. Organizations that don't measure quality systematically either overspend on delivery (encoding at higher bitrates than necessary) or underdeliver on experience (encoding too aggressively without knowing it).

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement thorough video quality assessment

choices.title: Optimize encoder settings based on content type

helpfulResource.displayText: Traditional encoding allocates the same target bit rate regardless of content complexity. Low-complexity content receives more bits than it needs while complex content may not receive enough. Content-aware encoding analyzes source complexity and allocates bits accordingly, delivering equivalent perceptual quality at lower average bitrates. The bit rate reduction translates directly to proportional savings in CDN delivery cost for every viewer session.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize encoder settings based on content type

questions.description: Region selection determines the baseline environmental cost of a streaming service. The energy mix of the Region and the distance content travels to viewers are fixed before any other optimization takes effect.

choices.title: Optimize regional distribution of streaming workloads to reduce resource waste and non-renewable energy use

helpfulResource.displayText: Place streaming workloads in the Regions that best balance proximity to viewers against the carbon intensity of the location. Region selection sets a floor on the environmental cost of a streaming service, because the energy mix of the Region and the distance content travels to viewers are decided before any other optimization takes effect.

questions.description: Streaming demand varies by orders of magnitude across the day and across events. Infrastructure sized for a theoretical peak sits idle most of its life.

choices.title: Implement adaptive infrastructure scaling based on viewer patterns

helpfulResource.displayText: Provision streaming infrastructure to follow actual viewer demand rather than a fixed peak assumption. Streaming demand is highly variable across the day, the week, and individual events, so capacity sized for the highest conceivable peak spends most of its life idle, consuming resources for an audience that isn't watching.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement adaptive infrastructure scaling based on viewer patterns

questions.title: How do you optimize your streaming software and architecture for sustainability?
questions.description: Every avoidable bit in an encode is multiplied across millions of viewing sessions in network transfer and client decode energy.

choices.title: Implement efficient encoding and delivery mechanisms

helpfulResource.displayText: Encode and deliver streaming media so that each viewer receives acceptable quality at the lowest practical bit rate. Encoding and delivery dominate the resource footprint of a streaming workload, because every avoidable bit is multiplied across millions of viewer sessions in transcode compute, network transfer, and client decode energy. Reducing bit rate to the minimum that delivers acceptable quality is the primary sustainability action in encoding and delivery.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement efficient encoding and delivery mechanisms

questions.title: How do you optimize your live streaming architecture for sustainability?
questions.description: Live workflow resource cost is governed by event duration and concurrent audience rather than catalog size. Channels that run idle between events or default to ultra-low latency for every stream consume resources without corresponding value.

choices.title: Design efficient, scalable live streaming workflows

helpfulResource.displayText: Run live streaming workflows so that processing resources are provisioned for the duration and audience of each event, not held continuously at peak capacity. Live workloads are uniquely wasteful when left running between events or over-provisioned for a latency target the use case doesn't need, because encode and packaging resources are consumed for the whole window whether viewers are watching.

improvementPlan.displayText: Design efficient, scalable live streaming workflows

questions.description: Media catalogs grow continuously. Masters, mezzanines, renditions, and archives accumulate, and storage becomes a steadily rising resource cost unless tiering and lifecycle rules tie retention to actual use.

choices.title: Implement intelligent storage tiering and content lifecycle management

helpfulResource.displayText: Store streaming media so that each asset occupies the storage tier its access pattern justifies, and retire assets when their value ends. Media catalogs grow without bound, masters, mezzanines, deliverable renditions, and archives accumulate, so storage becomes a steadily rising resource cost unless tiering and lifecycle rules tie retention to actual use.

questions.title: How do you minimize data movement in your streaming architecture?

choices.title: Optimize data flow and caching strategies

helpfulResource.displayText: Move streaming media as few times and as short a distance as possible. Every transfer of media data carries transfer energy and often triggers duplicate downstream processing, so a workload that copies content across Regions, re-fetches from origin on every request, or shuttles intermediate files between processing stages consumes resources out of proportion to the value delivered.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize data flow and caching strategies

questions.description: A self-managed component provisioned for one team's peak sits idle most of the time. Managed services aggregate demand across customers and scale to match, reaching higher average utilization.

choices.title: use AWS managed services for efficient resource utilization

helpfulResource.displayText: Use managed services in place of self-operated equivalents wherever a workload fits one. Managed services share infrastructure across many customers and scale with demand, so they reach a far higher average utilization than a self-managed component that each team provisions for its own peak and leaves idle the rest of the time.

questions.title: How do you incorporate sustainability into your development and deployment processes?
questions.description: The engineering process behind a streaming service carries its own resource footprint, dominated by idle non-production environments.

choices.title: Adopt sustainable development and deployment practices

helpfulResource.displayText: Run the development and deployment process so that it consumes resources only when work is actually happening. Build fleets, test environments, and non-production stacks are often left running indefinitely, so the engineering process behind a streaming service can carry a large, invisible resource footprint that has nothing to do with serving viewers.

questions.title: How do you drive ongoing improvement in sustainability for your streaming workloads?
questions.description: Without measurement and ownership, sustainability improvements are one-time efforts that decay.

choices.title: Establish sustainability KPIs and ongoing optimization processes

helpfulResource.displayText: Measure the sustainability of your streaming workload with metrics you can actually obtain, assign ownership for acting on them, and review them on a regular cadence. Without measurement and accountability, sustainability improvements are one-time efforts that decay as the catalog, audience, and architecture change.
